editorial:
Ever wonder how the old teachers at the witcher school actually started out? You get to follow a young Vesemir, who grows up poor and fights hard to become a monster hunter. The vibe is gritty and dark, but it has that classic fantasy feel where magic is dangerous and monsters are everywhere. It is a great origin story that shows you the hard training and the tough choices these fighters have to make just to survive in a world that hates them.

The action scenes are the best part because they move fast and look sharp. You will love how the fight choreography flows, though the story can feel a bit rushed in the middle. If you have a high-end TV, you should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Netflix to see all the detail in the animation. If you are a fan of collecting movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move. It is a perfect pick for you if you enjoy fast fights and dark fantasy worlds.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a big fight where Vesemir discovers that the monster he is hunting is actually his own brother. His brother became a twisted creature after trying to gain too much power. Vesemir has to make the hard choice to kill him to save others. After the battle, Vesemir decides to dedicate his life to teaching new witchers at Kaer Morhen so they can be better and kinder than the people who came before them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves monster hunting and epic fantasy battles.
